newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Wednesday after the U.S. currency rose to a 30-month high against the mark in world markets, dealers said.

"The Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market on a relatively big scale to prevent the basket from falling by more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The shekel declined as the dollar rose sharply against the mark. The rise of the dollar abroad pushed the basket downwards," he said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
The central bank has intervened in three of the last five trading sessions in a bid to keep the basket rate within the band.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2680 shekels against 3.2590 shekels on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6185 shekels against 3.6172 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7835 shekels per 100 yen versus 2.7993 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0451 shekels versus 2.0562 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2680 shekels.
